title: Dow Plummets 800 Points as Anthropic IPO Sparks Profit-Taking Frenzy – Live Updates】
body:
Wall Street jolted Thursday as the Dow Jones Industrial Average slumped more than 800 points, a decline that reflected a wave of profit‑taking sparked by the much‑anticipated Nasdaq debut of artificial‑intelligence start‑up Anthropic. The technology firm, backed by a consortium of high‑profile investors and a strategic partnership with a leading cloud provider, opened at a valuation that placed it among the most valuable AI‑focused IPOs in recent memory. While the offering itself was largely successful, the market’s reaction underscored lingering caution among traders who are balancing enthusiasm for AI growth with concerns about broader economic headwinds.

The tumble in the Dow was not isolated to technology stocks; it rippled through sectors ranging from consumer discretionary to industrials, pulling the index down 1.1 percent by the close. Futures for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 mirrored the downward trajectory, suggesting that the sell‑off could extend into the next trading session. Analysts pointed to the timing of Anthropic’s listing—just weeks after a series of mixed corporate earnings reports and amid ongoing geopolitical uncertainties—as a catalyst that amplified traders’ appetite for short‑term gains. “When a high‑profile IPO like Anthropic hits the market, it creates a temporary surge of buying pressure that can quickly reverse as investors lock in profits,” said a senior market strategist at a major brokerage firm.

Beyond the immediate market reaction, the IPO highlighted the accelerating competition within the AI space. Anthropic, founded by former OpenAI researchers, has positioned itself as a “responsible AI” company, emphasizing safety and alignment in its product roadmap. Its entry onto the Nasdaq adds a new heavyweight to a field already crowded with firms such as OpenAI’s partner Microsoft, Alphabet’s DeepMind, and a host of niche startups. The influx of capital into AI ventures has been fueled by both venture‑capital enthusiasm and corporate demand for generative‑AI tools, but the sector’s rapid expansion also raises questions about regulatory oversight and the sustainability of current valuations.

Meanwhile, macroeconomic undercurrents continued to shape market sentiment. In Europe, the governor of France’s central bank addressed the lingering fiscal stalemate in a televised interview, expressing confidence that a budget for the upcoming year would eventually be agreed upon despite deep partisan divides. His reassurance was aimed at calming fears that a prolonged political impasse could exacerbate sovereign‑debt concerns and spill over into global markets. However, investors remain wary, noting that fiscal uncertainty in the eurozone could intersect with tighter monetary policies in the United States, where the Federal Reserve is expected to maintain its restrictive stance through the end of the year.

The confluence of these factors—AI‑driven hype, profit‑taking dynamics, and geopolitical‑economic uncertainty—creates a complex backdrop for investors navigating the current landscape. Some market participants are adopting a more defensive posture, shifting assets into defensive sectors such as utilities and consumer staples, while others see the dip as a buying opportunity in high‑growth areas. “The key is to differentiate between short‑term volatility and the longer‑term structural shifts that AI is bringing to the economy,” noted an equity analyst at an international investment bank.

Looking ahead, the market’s trajectory will likely hinge on several variables. The performance of Anthropic’s stock in its early trading days will serve as a barometer for investor appetite toward AI IPOs, while upcoming earnings reports from major tech firms will test the resilience of the sector’s growth narrative. Additionally, the resolution of fiscal negotiations in France and broader European fiscal policy could either bolster confidence or reignite concerns about fiscal sustainability. As traders weigh these intersecting forces, the coming weeks will reveal whether today’s sharp correction is a fleeting reaction or the beginning of a more pronounced recalibration in equity markets.
